sub_services.name: Search Visibility Audit
sub_services.outcome: A clear, ranked picture of where the business is and isn't being found — across Google, AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Bing Chat — and which gap closes first for the most return.
sub_services.shape: Diagnostic engagement before any optimisation work. Maps directly to diff_correct_scoping — diagnosis before prescription.

sub_services.name: SEO (traditional)
sub_services.outcome: Right people finding the business through Google search, with the right intent, and converting once they land.
sub_services.shape: Keyword research focused on high-intent terms, technical SEO audit and remediation, on-page optimisation, local SEO (Google My Business, NAP consistency, regional Victoria geo-targeting), performance tracking with honest reporting (no ranking guarantees — outcome reporting only).

sub_services.name: GEO / AEO — AI search visibility
sub_services.outcome: The business gets cited and surfaced by ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Bing Chat — not just blue-link Google. Brand becomes part of the answer, not just an option in the list.
sub_services.shape: Schema implementation (FAQPage, HowTo, Speakable, QAPage, organization, author, product), answer-first content restructure, citation-ready content design, cross-platform monitoring of brand mentions in AI environments, entity signal alignment (consistent naming across website, LinkedIn, directories, knowledge graph). Continuous refresh — AI citations decay if not maintained.

sub_services.name: Content for humans and AI
sub_services.outcome: Content that earns its read from a human AND gets cited by an answer engine. One asset, two audiences — neither shortchanged.
sub_services.shape: Topic clustering for topical authority, connected content series rather than isolated posts, 50-word answer summaries that lead each major section, question-based headings, evidence-backed insights, first-party authoritative content rather than rephrased web. Content is shaped so it can be cited verbatim by AI without losing the human read.

sub_services.name: Digital PR in AI ecosystems
sub_services.outcome: The business shows up in the places AI engines learn from — credible mentions, citations, and presence across the surfaces (LinkedIn, YouTube, podcasts, community spaces, industry publications) that AI training and retrieval pull from.
sub_services.shape: Outreach + presence-building strategy, brand-mention tracking, expansion across video/audio/long-form/social — measured by how often and how positively the brand is referenced in AI answers, not just by traditional backlinks.

sub_services.name: Search visibility measurement
sub_services.outcome: Honest reporting on what's working — including the new metrics (AI citations, sentiment, salience) alongside traditional rankings and Search Console data. No vanity metrics; outcomes only.
sub_services.shape: Continuous tracking of brand mentions in ChatGPT/Perplexity/AI Overviews, alignment with Search Console + GA4, sentiment vs salience monitoring (how brand is talked about, not just how often), translated into a quarterly read of 'is this working' against business goals.

framing_notes: Buildio's marketing isn't standalone — it integrates with svc_software (the systems it surfaces), svc_business_transformation (the goals it serves), svc_streamlining (the operational reality behind it), and svc_automations (the workflows that scale it). Marketing service offered in isolation is weaker than marketing tied to the rest of Buildio.

Specifically: Buildio competes differently from a pure-play SEO/GEO agency (e.g. Arcadian Digital — Melbourne-based, narrower scope). Arcadian is a stronger choice if marketing is the *only* thing the business needs help with. Buildio is the choice when the business needs the marketing AND the systems behind it to actually grow.

angles.angle: Diagnosis before prescription. A partner pitching a solution on the first call is guessing — and prescription without diagnosis is malpractice.

source_inspiration.from: Andrew Dunn (CEO & Chief AI Officer, '450+ Companies'), LinkedIn post 'Yes. I eat Kit Kats like this.'
source_inspiration.lifted_verbatim: If your AI consultant pitches a solution on the first call, they're guessing. Prescription without diagnosis is malpractice.
source_inspiration.use_note: Don't lift verbatim. Paraphrase into Buildio voice — connects to diff_correct_scoping. The 'malpractice' framing is sharp; consider whether to soften.

angles.angle: Most businesses don't need AI — they need their processes fixed first. AI on broken processes just breaks them faster.

source_inspiration.from: Andrew Dunn, same Kit Kat post — points 1 and 7.
lifted_verbatim_pieces: Most companies don't need AI. They need their processes fixed first.
AI won't save your business. It'll just break it faster. Fix the foundation first.
source_inspiration.use_note: Strong fit for Buildio — streamlining service explicitly addresses this. Differentiation against 'AI consultancies' that lead with the AI hammer.

angles.angle: Don't bite the whole transformation in one go. One workflow at a time. Break the change into pieces and deliver each piece end-to-end.

source_inspiration.from: Andrew Dunn Kit Kat post — point 6.
source_inspiration.lifted_verbatim: Most companies trying to implement AI are doing the same thing I'm doing with this Kit Kat. Trying to bite the whole thing at once instead of breaking it into pieces. One workflow at a time. One finger at a time.
source_inspiration.use_note: Excellent metaphor (Kit Kat). Don't reuse the metaphor — Buildio needs its own — but the structural angle (incremental, one workflow at a time) is portable.

angles.angle: AI changed how your people work; org design hasn't caught up. That widening gap is where the structural and economic upside sits — closing it is the work.

source_inspiration.from: David Chinn (CEO & Co-Founder, Lexer), LinkedIn post.
lifted_verbatim_pieces: AI has changed how you and your people work. However organisation design hasn't caught up.
That gap is widening every week. Closing it is where the structural and economic upside sits.
find the constraints hiding in your own org chart
source_inspiration.use_note: Powerful framing for Buildio's transformation work. The constraints-hiding-in-the-org-chart line is particularly strong. Paraphrase into Buildio voice.

angles.angle: AI increases productivity, but it also increases the complexity of the systems behind that productivity. You need people who can manage and maintain the robots — that's a new skill, and most businesses don't have it yet.

source_inspiration.from: Thomas Mackenzie (Director of Client Services, Scale by Avec), via TechDay Australia.
source_inspiration.lifted_verbatim: We need to remember that AI does increase productivity, but it also increases the complexity of the systems and delivery... [you'll] need people to manage and maintain the robots. It's a different skill that people will need to learn.
source_inspiration.use_note: Buildio's natural counter-position: 'Buildio manages the robots for you while your team learns to.' Combines the 'sensational support' concept with the technical capability.

decisions_log.decision: Ported the UPHQ SEO plugin to Buildio (buildio-seo, ProfessionalService schema, Ballarat local SEO signals, Yoast suppression with Yoast-meta passthrough). Activated locally, then deployed to production via rsync and activated remotely via wp-cli. Verified head output and schema rendering on both environments.
decisions_log.rationale: Buildio.au needs proper GEO/AEO foundations to be cited by AI engines (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) and proper SEO foundations to be found via traditional search. UPHQ already had a battle-tested single-file plugin doing both — porting beats writing from scratch. Local-first activation + dry-run rsync + remote backup of active_plugins gave a safe rollback path.
decisions_log.rsync_filter_change: Added '+ public_html/wp-content/plugins/buildio-seo/***' to _rsync/.rsync_all (the filter is whitelist-style; plugins are excluded by default).
decisions_log.wp_config_change: wp-config.php was also pushed (the dotenv-block guards we added earlier today). Behaviour is identical to the un-guarded version in web context; the guards only matter for WP-CLI bootstrap idempotency.

decisions_log.decision: Created content-offering-positioning.json as the structured brain for Buildio.au content and positioning, scoped narrower than the Midlands full-project brain (this brain is content/offering/positioning only; app/domain knowledge live in their own .claude/ folders).
decisions_log.rationale: Markdown handles narrative well but doesn't structure cross-references (audience → page → angle). JSON gives a queryable, versionable, growable map for content development without the markdown becoming a tangle of cross-links.

open_questions.question: What does Buildio.au actually sell? Service shape (project / retainer / advisory), typical deliverable, who buys, price range. Required to populate offering.* and positioning.*.
open_questions.answered_so_far: Five service categories named (added marketing + automations to the original three on 2026-05-07): software/digital systems, business transformation, streamlining, marketing, automations. Aim statement captured: support businesses to grow and achieve goals through great digital systems, with sensational support/advice/skill/expertise as the tone.
open_questions.still_open: Per-category detail (what software exactly, what kind of transformation, what kind of streamlining, what kind of marketing, what kind of automations), engagement shape (project / retainer / advisory / fractional), typical deliverable, who buys, price range, geographic focus within Australia.

open_questions.question: Does 'software' in Buildio's offering refer to (a) selling/promoting Rohan's own software products (like UniPixel) under the Buildio umbrella, (b) custom software development as a service for clients, or (c) both? Affects how Buildio.au relates to unipixelhq.com and how the Software service is framed on the site.
open_questions.answered: Primarily (b) — 'Advanced software development solutions focused on ROI' confirms the service framing is custom development for clients. Doesn't rule out (c); UniPixel could still appear on Buildio.au as one of Rohan's own products, but it's not the central Software offer. The headline is bespoke ROI-driven development.
open_questions.still_open: Whether/how UniPixel and other own products are positioned on Buildio.au — sibling brand mention, products portfolio, neither?

open_questions.question: Who are the concrete prospect personas — by role, sector, company size, where they're searching, what brought them here? Required before audiences[] can be populated and before pages can be cross-referenced to audiences.

What are Buildio.au's actual competitors / alternatives the prospect considers? Big-4 (Deloitte/PwC etc.), boutique consultancies (named), in-house build, freelance, SaaS-only, status quo? Each needs a record with strength + where Buildio wins.

What's already on buildio.au — page titles, hero copy, sections, current CTAs? An extraction pass against the live site or local theme content (inc/home/* partials) populates pages[] with the current state as a starting baseline before iteration.
What is the single canonical CTA across the site? ('Book a discovery call', 'Talk to Buildio', etc.) Drives the writing-style.md placeholder and content_versions.ctas[].
